identity:
A common question is, why does JUNIPER GOLD have a specific combat-focused division and COPPER PRIME does not?  There are two main reasons.

The first is that fire spreads.  The use of JUNIPER GOLD poses little extra risk unless an incautious mathematician causes structural damage sufficient to induce a collapse.  Any use of COPPER PRIME can start a fire, and the ability to extinguish fires is far from universal among COPPER PRIME mathematicians.

The second is the short range.  This is a consistent problem with all mathematics, but the danger of uncontrolled COPPER PRIME usage provides an extra disadvantage.

In essence, COPPER PRIME has many of the same disadvantages of flamethrowers that led to them no longer being used in active service without few advantages to counteract this; primarily a lack of fuel requirements.  Unless the range problem is solved, military applications of COPPER PRIME will always take a secondary role behind JUNIPER GOLD.

identity:
arsongirl.mp3

Incredibly this is footage of the Cataclysm during the height of the portal storms.  It looks like Bar Harbor, Maine.  Some kind of godzilla sized squid lashes the docks with tentacles hundreds of feet long, while a Heritage class Coast Guard cutter fires its 57mm naval gun at the giant squid.

That is the background of the footage.  The foreground is at the top of the hill overlooking the road down to the docks.  Here people have taken shelter in stores on the main road down to the docks, but a young girl with bloodshot eyes giggles as she walks towards a storefront.  Her clothes are singed and the air around them shimmers like a summer heat haze.  Suddenly she squeals in delight as flames erupt from her arms and engulf the storefront.  She moves from one store to the next working her way down to the chaos of the docks, driving fleeing civilians from their shelter or melting the flesh from their bones when they move too slowly.

identity:
You're fuckin' right it's a proper setup, but damn, I could say the same about you!  Look at ya'!"  The Doc walks over to the spider-like surgical robot, and pats the soft, cushioned examination table.  He wipes his brow with his sleeve and gulps.  "Right.  Hop up here, and let's plug into your interface there, and see what we're working with.  I suspect we'll have to swap it out."  The Doc then starts to unclasp a set of wrist and ankle ties attached to the exam table.

"Hope this is alright.  We'll tie down your limbs.  Never worked on… well… someone like you, before.  Guess I haven't worked on that many people in any case.  No worries.  I can do it.  Just don't want you, uh, bugging out and hurting yourself, got it?
